newsitem.title: USA: Crestar to acquire American National.
newsitem.headline: Crestar to acquire American National.

text.p: Crestar Financial Corp. said Monday it agreed to acquire American National Bancorp Inc., another Baltimore, Md.-based banking company, in a deal valued at about $72.9 million.
Under the definitive agreement, Crestar will offer $20.25 in cash or stock for each of American National's 3.6 million shares outstanding in a tax-free exchange.
The company said it intends to purchase in the open market any Crestar shares used in the transaction.
American National shot up $3.125 to $19.25 on Nasdaq after the announcement, while Crestar's stock fell 87.5 cents to $40.375 on the New York Stock Exchange shortly before midday.

American National is the holding company for American National Savings Bank, a thrift institution with $505 million in assets, deposits of $330 million and 10 branches in the Baltimore metropolitan area.
American National will become part of Crestar's Maryland Region, which includes 35 branches.
Crestar, a subsidiary of the $22.8 billion-asset Crestar Financial Corp., has 477 offices in Maryland, Washington, D.C, and Virginia.
The merger is expected to close during the fourth quarter, subject to approval by regulators and American National shareholders.
Crestar has an option to buy an additional 792,000 American National shares if the deal fails to close under certain conditions.
Crestar said it expects to combine American National branches, employees, customer accounts and computer systems with Crestar's operations over five months.
